questions.stem: Most Common extranodal site of Lymphoma in HIV is?
questions.solutionHtml:
CNS

Most common extranodal site for Lymphoma in:

  • General population: GIT (stomach).
  • HIV patients: CNS.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 570, 1450

questions.stem: Neoplastic cells with multilobulated nuclei (cloverleaf or flower cells) are seen in-
questions.solutionHtml:
Adult T cell leukaemia
  • Adult T-Cell Leukaemia/Lymphoma
  • This neoplasm of CD4+ T cells is only observed in adults infected by human T-cell leukaemia retrovirus type 1(HTLV-1)
  • Common findings include skin lesions, generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, peripheral blood lymphocytosis, and hypercalcemia.
  • Tumour cells with multilobulated nuclei (“cloverleaf” or “flower” cells).
  • Most patients present with a rapidly progressive disease that is fatal within months to 1 year despite aggressive chemotherapy.
  • Less commonly, the tumour involves only the skin and follows a much more indolent course, like that of mycosis fungoides


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 605, 606, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 771

questions.stem: The Commonest site for extranodal lymphoma is-
questions.solutionHtml:
Stomach
  • The commonest site for extranodal lymphoma is the Stomach
  • The gastrointestinal tract is the most common site for extranodal NHL (10 to 15% of all NHL).
  • The stomach accounts for 50% of gastrointestinal lymphomas
  • 60% of gastric lymphoma are aggressive, usually DLBCL, while 40% are low-grade, usually MALT type.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 570, 1450, Wintrobe's Clinical Hematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 2177

questions.stem: A patient of 70 years, presented with generalized lymphadenopathy. WBC count was 20,000/mm3 and blood film showed 70% mature-looking lymphocytes. Next investigation that should be done:
questions.solutionHtml:
Peripheral blood Immunophenotyping
  • In the given question, an elderly patient with generalized lymphadenopathy was found to have a WBC count of 20,000/mm3 and blood film showed >70% mature-looking lymphocytes i.e. Peripheral smear has been done and is showing leukocytosis, with mature lymphocytes.
  • Most likely this is a case of Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma with spillover in the peripheral blood.
  • (Microscopy of Hodgkin’s lymphoma shows Reed Sternberg cells in a reactive background).
  • NHLs can be identified on the basis of immunophenotyping:


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 597-604

Leukocyte common antigen
  • Since Lymphoma arises from mature leukocytes, Lymphoma cells are positive for Leukocyte common antigen (CD45).


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 593

questions.stem: The international prognostic index for lymphomas includes the following prognostic factors, except:

options.label: B
options.text: Number of extra lymphatic sites involved

questions.solutionHtml:
Hemoglobin and albumin
  • International prognostic index for lymphomas do not include Hemoglobin and albumin


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 774.

CD34 - ve & Surface Ig +ve
  • In Burkitt Lymphoma CD34 - ve & Surface Ig +ve
  • CD34 is positive in Hematopoietic stem cells
  • Classical triad of Burkitt’s lymphoma:
  • CD19 +ve, Surface Ig +ve and CD34 - ve


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 601, 602, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 775

options.label: D

questions.solutionHtml:
B cell lymphoma
  • Burkitt’s lymphoma is a B-cell lymphoma, which can present as an abdominal mass


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 601, 602, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 775

questions.stem: The most malignant form of NHL is -
questions.solutionHtml:
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
  • Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the most aggressive lymphoma.
  • Follicular lymphomas are low-grade and indolent.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 600, 601
